messages.subject: Dynamic Energy Budget Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,

For those of you interested in DEB theory, I've made a prototype Shiny app that allows you to simulate growth trajectories at different temperatures and food levels for most of the ~2800 species currently in the DEB parameter database collection. It is essentially running the 'rundeb' function of NicheMapR. The main purpose is educational.

http://bioforecasts.science.unimelb.edu.au/app_direct/deb/

Any feedback welcome - there are bound to be some bugs and issues!

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Errors while runing DEB model tutorial
messages.subject_clean: Errors while runing DEB model tutorial
messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

Sorry - I've since change some things and haven't updated that tutorial. I'll fix it up but in the meantime you should set the shade this way:

minshades <- micro$minshade   # min available shade?
maxshades <- micro$maxshade # max available shade?

and you should indeed remove F_m (maximum surface area-specific searching rate, # particles per time) and replace it with p_Xm (maximum surface area-specific intake rate, J per time) which you can set to something large e.g. p.Am * 5 (i.e. five times the maximum assimilation rate). In the standard DEB model, p_Xm should be p.Am / kap_X, i.e. the maximum assimilation rate divided by the digestive efficiency. However, because there's a stomach, the intake rate can be much faster than the assimilation rate. If you just make it very large, your simulation will be limited by handling time = digestion and not by searching rate. Hope that makes sense.

All the best,
Mike
